question.text: Bluewave Capital AIF is structured as a trust. The sponsor has proposed that Mr. Rajesh Gupta — who is an independent director of the investment management company — also be appointed as a trustee of the AIF. Is this permissible?

answer.text: Yes, independent directors are specifically allowed to double as trustees for governance efficiency
No — the trustee CANNOT be the manager, director (including independent director), officer, or employee of the investment management company
Yes, provided the investor advisory committee ratifies the dual role
Yes, but only for Cat I AIFs; Cat II trust structures prohibit it

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012, the trustee cannot be the manager, director (including independent director), officer or employee of an investment management company. This wall between trustee and IM preserves fiduciary independence — the trustee must ensure transactions are compliant with scheme objectives without structural conflicts. The Trap: The 'independent directors allowed' option is a common trap — candidates assume 'independent' directors escape the bar, but the PDF explicitly includes 'including independent director'. The IAC-ratification option invents an override. The Cat I-vs-Cat II option invents a distinction not in the regulations. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same prohibition. XXI-B (Portfolio Manager) has no trustee concept. XV (Research Analyst) tests independence standards in a different context (research vs investment banking). Manager's Pro-Tip: When structuring a new AIF trust, map your proposed trustee panel against the IM's director/officer roster EARLY — a last-minute disqualification delays SEBI registration. A common clean solution is to appoint a SEBI-registered trustee company (like IDBI Trusteeship, Axis Trustee) with no overlap.
